patch_resolves_note: The fixed original reaches the same protected Message::Write path on the original PoC, satisfies the reset obligation at target_tlv_reuse_root, and preserves only the fixed-size outbound Target TLV copy request into the sink.

nodes.description: At the outbound append site, the serialized size of aTargetTlv exceeds the concrete ThreadTargetTlv object size because the response reuses the inbound TLV header length.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace satisfies `target_tlv_append.append_size > target_tlv_append.fixed_size`, while the fixed original refutes that inequality after resetting the TLV length.

nodes.description: At the Message::Write sink, the target-TLV copy request reaching memcpy is the same serialized size computed for the outbound response append.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable and fixed assertion traces both satisfy `target_tlv_append.append_size == target_tlv_memcpy_sink.copy_request_size`, showing that the sink memcpy consumes the append-derived request length.

edges.description: The inbound Target TLV length preserved in HandleAddressQuery is carried unchanged into the outbound response append as aTargetTlv.GetLength().
edges.evidence: The vulnerable and fixed assertion traces both satisfy `target_tlv_reuse_root.target_length == target_tlv_append.target_length`.

edges.description: The serialized Target TLV size computed at the append site becomes the copy-request length consumed by Message::Write.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable and fixed assertion traces both satisfy `target_tlv_append.append_size == target_tlv_memcpy_sink.copy_request_size`.

root_cause_criterion.description: Before HandleAddressQuery reuses targetTlv as an outbound response TLV, targetTlv.GetLength() must be reset to the fixed payload length `sizeof(targetTlv) - sizeof(ThreadTlv)` instead of preserving the inbound header length.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original violates `target_tlv_reuse_root.target_length == target_tlv_reuse_root.fixed_length` while still reaching the protected write event, and the fixed original satisfies the same predicate genuinely on that protected path.
